problems.stem: You finish a draft and ask ETHOBOT, "Did I pass?" Why is this the wrong question for the tutor?
options: ETHOBOT only answers questions typed in all capital letters.
ETHOBOT is a practice and feedback tutor; your instructor and the rubric assign the official grade, so ask for feedback instead.
ETHOBOT can grade but charges for it.
Passing questions must be emailed, not typed.
problems.explanation: The tutor helps you prepare and revise; it does not set the official grade. Ask for actionable feedback, not a verdict.

problems.stem: Which request gives ETHOBOT enough to give you useful, specific feedback?
options: help
Here is my resume bullet: "Helped with events." Does it have an action verb and a measurable result, and how would you tighten it?
is this good?
fix it
problems.explanation: A useful request states the goal, includes the artifact, and names what you want checked. Vague prompts get vague answers.

problems.stem: Which message keeps your use of ETHOBOT inside its intended role as a tutor?
options: Write my whole discussion post and I will paste it in.
Point out two places where my discussion post lacks supporting evidence so I can fix them myself.
Submit this post to the gradebook for me.
Tell me the exact grade I will receive.
problems.explanation: Asking for targeted feedback you then act on keeps the work and judgment yours. Asking the tutor to author or submit it does not.

problems.stem: ETHOBOT gives you three suggestions. You apply two and ignore one because it would make a false claim. What does a complete critique log record?
options: Only the two changes you made.
All three: the two you accepted (with what you changed) and the one you rejected, with a one-line reason for each.
Just a note that you talked to the tutor.
Only the suggestion you rejected, since that was the hard call.
problems.explanation: A complete log shows accepted, modified, and rejected suggestions with reasons, so a reader can audit your judgment.

problems.stem: The tutor suggests replacing your resume line 'helped organize the volunteer program' with 'managed the entire volunteer program.' You coordinated one of its three committees. Which log entry is right?
options: Accept: the tutor's version is stronger and recruiters like strong verbs.
Reject: the suggestion touched your wording, so the whole idea is unusable.
Modify: keep the stronger verb but trim to the defensible scope, e.g. 'coordinated one of three committees in the volunteer program,' and log what you changed and why.
Accept now, and plan to soften it if anyone asks.
problems.explanation: The suggestion is directionally right (the original undersells) but overreaches (you did not manage the entire program). The modify move keeps the improvement while keeping the claim defensible, and the log records the trim so a reviewer can see the judgment, not just the outcome.
